original_test_intent: Verify that a supported HDD/SSD absent from a slot at boot can be hot-added, correctly enumerated and exercised for five minutes without unexpected OS or iMM/BMC errors.
original_method: A qualified operator inserts the approved drive into the exact supported empty bay while the agent timestamps the event, captures complete Windows or Linux enumeration, runs only the approved identity-bound five-minute workload and preserves full OS and management logs.
manual_activity: User approves the hot-add/data/workload plan; qualified operator inserts the exact drive; agent captures enumeration, runs the approved five-minute I/O and collects complete logs.
required_inputs: Windows or Linux target path and supported OS/build
Drive stable ID, empty slot/backplane/controller mapping and hot-add support
Meaning of the four-second insertion step and operator procedure
Approved isolated five-minute I/O workload and data boundary
Backup, iMM/BMC access, OOB/console and removal/retention recovery
safety_requirements: Verify the bay is hot-swap capable and empty at boot before insertion
Confirm drive and slot identity and ensure the new target is not boot, production or unknown storage
Preserve existing logs and collect the full insertion interval
Stop on resistance, wrong identity, unexpected RAID/mount state, I/O/filesystem/media/thermal/iMM error or access loss
Do not power the bay, insert/remove hardware, write an unspecified device or repair/reboot automatically
agent_execution_scope: Capture empty-slot and all-disk baseline with stable identities
Record insertion timestamp and complete Windows Disk Management/Event Viewer or Linux lsblk/fdisk/kernel evidence
Run and track the approved five-minute I/O only after target validation
Collect final health/iMM/BMC state; do not perform physical actions or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve hot-add support, exact drive/slot, OS/workload/data and recovery plan
Provide a qualified operator and own removal/retention decision
Review enumeration, workload and complete OS/iMM evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsblk is useful on Linux, but insecure SSH and tail-only dmesg do not cover Windows, the empty-at-boot condition, stable slot identity, five-minute I/O or full iMM/BMC evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture full OS-specific disk inventory and event/log evidence before and after the operator insertion, then run a tracked five-minute approved workload on the exact new drive/volume with health and iMM/BMC monitoring.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Empty-at-boot slot, four-second insertion step, Windows/Linux paths, five-minute I/O and source 15/80 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a single identity-locked hot-add event with synchronized physical, enumeration, workload, health and management-log evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact target safety, cross-layer evidence and recovery ownership while preserving the manual insertion and five-minute stress.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation assists observation and workload only; it cannot establish physical insertion correctness by itself.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: New device names can change and automatic mount/RAID policies may act asynchronously; stable IDs and complete controller/OS state are required.

project_override_considerations: If Windows and Linux are both required rather than alternative platform paths, they need separate approved boot images and evidence runs; one OS must not silently cover the other.
expected_evidence: Operator/date, insertion timestamp and photo/video if permitted
Complete pre/post stable-ID Windows or Linux enumeration
Exact five-minute workload, target, PID, output, exit status and health telemetry
Complete Windows events or Linux dmesg/syslog/SEL plus iMM/BMC logs
Final drive/slot/RAID/mount state, retention/removal and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently defines one manual hot-add followed by enumeration, I/O and logs; DeepSeek is incomplete but does not create an irreducible source ambiguity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Hot-swap support, operator, workload and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites; purpose and review are clear.

review_improvement: Restores the empty-at-boot and five-minute workload checkpoints and requires complete OS/iMM evidence around one exact physical insertion.
independent_technical_reasoning: Hot-add success is a state transition, not a static lsblk result: the slot must be absent at boot, then the same stable drive must appear through controller and OS layers, sustain bounded I/O and leave management logs clean. Short log tails and volatile device names can miss delayed errors or misidentify the inserted drive, so synchronized complete evidence is necessary.
